Descriptive estimates and 95% confidence intervals

Methods

Data. NDWS Assisted Living staff survey.

Weighting. Every percentage uses FinalWeight, so estimates describe the national assisted-living workforce rather than the sample. Each percentage is computed among respondents with a valid answer to that item: legitimate skips, refusals (including Wave 1 positive refusal codes), don’t-know, not-displayed and disclosure-masked values are excluded from the denominator, never counted as “no”. Median earnings use all valid reported yearly earnings of $0 or more.

Geography. The PUF has no state identifier. Sampling area comes from the sampling stratum (user guide, Table 8). Strata 1–12 cross facility size with Census region, and the design merges the Northeast with the Midwest. Strata 13 (rural, low deprivation) and 14 (high Area Deprivation Index) pool facilities from every region, so they are listed beside the map rather than drawn on it. States are shaded by the region they belong to; the map does not show state-level estimates.

Source and license. Maust, Donovan; Spetz, Joanne; Wagner, James; Marcus, Steven; and Wagner, Laura (2026). National Dementia Workforce Study (NDWS): Assisted Living Staff, Wave 2 (2025). ICPSR. E251473V1. Dataset-derived results: CC BY-SA 4.0. The National Dementia Workforce Study data is sponsored by the National Institute on Aging (Grant U54AG084520) and is conducted by the University of Michigan and the University of California, San Francisco.

Small groups. Estimates with fewer than 30 valid responses are removed during the build, including population totals for small groups. For role composition, the entire breakdown and all role-specific weighted population totals and workforce shares in that sampling area are withheld if any role has fewer than 30 respondents. An additional sampling area is withheld when needed to prevent recovery from national role totals and other sampling areas, and likewise when a small area's total could be recovered from the national total. Respondent counts and otherwise reportable item percentages are retained. Other item percentages have no additional numerator threshold. Each estimate with 30–49 valid responses is flagged, including tenure subgroups. Respondent counts are shown to explain suppression.

95% confidence intervals. The charts and detailed table show every descriptive estimate, valid n and CI for the selected group. Shares use weighted ratio Taylor linearization over facility clusters, with t critical values (facilities minus one degrees of freedom). Earnings use Woodruff CDF inversion; population totals use facility sums. Strata and finite population corrections are omitted: these are approximate intervals, not full stratified survey intervals (user guide v4 §§3.4, 4). The design facility count G and t(G−1) degrees of freedom retain all positive-weight facilities, including zero-contribution domain facilities. Covered facilities count those with valid item/domain responses; single-facility domains with n≥30 have estimates and CIs withheld and carry a prominent coverage warning. Constant responses can yield degenerate linearized CIs. Equal earnings-quantile bounds can result from discrete or repeated values; both cases do not imply zero population uncertainty.

Model. Survey-weighted logistic regression of “very satisfied overall” (vs. anything less), fit on respondents with valid answers to every model item (the training and benefit counts require an answer to every topic or box), with facility-clustered standard errors (strata omitted; covariance support with variance weights is incomplete in statsmodels). The associations are cross-sectional and self-reported, so they do not show causation.
